Roles and Permissions states: 'promote-golden-baseline.sh itself refuses to run whenever the CI environment variable is set or when no --approved-by <human-identifier> flag is supplied ..., and AC-040's static check independently verifies CI's own .github/workflows/test.yml never references either mutation-capable command' -- explicitly framing the script's own runtime guard as a second, distinct enforcement mechanism alongside AC-040. Scanning all 40 AC/TEST rows in acceptance-tests.md, none exercises this runtime refusal (CI env var set, or --approved-by omitted, producing non-zero exit / no canonical write); AC-018/TEST-018 and AC-040/TEST-040 are both 'static / doc-review' checks of the manifest contract and the CI workflow text, not of the script's own fail-closed behavior. A task author decomposing Phase 2/3 tasks therefore has no acceptance criterion committing anyone to test this specific irreversible-change safety guard (canonical golden-baseline mutation, Security Boundaries B1), so a future edit that silently drops the guard from the script would go undetected by every currently-enumerated AC/TEST. This is a spec-review-scoped completeness gap in the AC list (not an implementation detail, since the guard's existence/behavior is already asserted as fact in requirements.md) with a high-risk claim (irreversible baseline-canonicalization boundary) and no planned validation surface, hence Major per calibration ('missing observable acceptance criterion... high-risk claim with no planned validation surface'); it stops short of Critical because the surrounding process (AC-018 human-reviewed-PR requirement, AC-040 CI-workflow scan) still makes most of the boundary testable and reviewable.

Every AC (AC-001-AC-040) has exactly one corresponding placeholder Test ID with no gaps, and the footnote at the end of acceptance-tests.md explicitly disambiguates package-level placeholder IDs from real per-suite-file case numbers (e.g. TEST-018/TEST-019) so no row is identifier-ambiguous. Main Workflows gives a numbered, unambiguous Phase 2/3 implementation sequence (steps 1-7), and forward-looking design decisions are consistently and explicitly deferred to design.md (a sibling Phase-1 artifact reviewed under a separate gate) rather than left unassigned. Aside from the single APPROVAL-BOUNDARY gap noted above, the package hands off cleanly without requiring a downstream reviewer to invent missing product behavior.
